title: Resolved lenderPrivateKey's on-chain signing address is never verified against loanRow.lender_wallet -- a fund-misattribution/wrong-payer risk whenever runWakeGate is invoked by an instance other than the selected lenderId
description:
wake-gate.mjs's own comment (lines 142-150) ASSERTS as fact that 'this wake ALWAYS runs under the LENDER's own per-instance env ... an instance can only ever sign as itself here, never another instance's'. This claim is NOT enforced anywhere in the code and is not even checked by any test. findSelectedPair (lines 77-101) scans the FULL shared citizens registry (candidateIds x candidateIds, both outer AND inner loop over the SAME registry-derived list) and returns the FIRST pair, independent of which identity is actually executing the current process. resolveLenderPrivateKey({env}) (line 162) then resolves whatever EVM key belongs to the CALLING process's own ANICCA_HOME (resolve-identity.mjs's fail-closed, self-scoped resolution -- confirmed correct in isolation) -- but nothing compares that resolved key's derived address to selectedPair.lenderId's own registered wallet (freshLender.walletAddress.evm / provisionalRow.lender_wallet, lending-orchestrator.mjs line 230). defaultDisburse (lending-orchestrator.mjs lines 169-176) forwards deps.lenderPrivateKey straight into payViaFacilitator -> signAuthorization (escrow.mjs lines 51-56), which derives `payer.address = privateKeyToAccount(privateKey).address` and signs a transferWithAuthorization FROM that derived address. The facilitator's /verify step checks THAT address's real chain balance, not the registry's `balanceUsd`. Nowhere is `payerAddress` (returned by payViaFacilitator, escrow.mjs line 164) ever compared against `loanRow.lender_wallet` before the ledger row is finalized (lending-orchestrator.mjs lines 241-258) -- confirmed via grep of the entire lending-orchestrator.mjs, zero hits for `payerAddress`.

Concretely: the REAL production registry (~/.hermes/state/citizens.json, verified live) has exactly two candidates, Franklin (homeDir=/Users/operator/.blockrun, wallet.evm=0x3EcCAD24794ca298D25378E9902A251322ea8749) and Franklin2 (homeDir=/Users/operator/.franklin2-home/.blockrun, wallet.evm=0xe7747Fd899D8987821Bb4CB3D6aDf22565F87ce9). economy/lending/run.sh (per its own header comment, mirroring self/spawn/run.sh's shape) is designed to be invoked on EACH citizen's OWN wake cadence, under that citizen's own env -- i.e. BOTH Franklin's and Franklin2's own cron/loop are expected to independently call `economy/lending/run.sh` -> `runWakeGate`. findSelectedPair is deterministic over the SAME shared registry+ledger, so whichever of the two instances wakes, it will independently compute the SAME selectedPair (currently {lenderId:'Franklin', borrowerId:'Franklin2'}, matching the real stuck loan_Franklin_1 row). If Franklin2's OWN wake invokes economy/lending/run.sh (under Franklin2's own ANICCA_HOME=/Users/operator/.franklin2-home/.blockrun), resolveLenderPrivateKey({env}) resolves FRANKLIN2's own EVM key -- NOT Franklin's -- while the ledger row is still stamped lender_id:'Franklin', lender_wallet:Franklin's address. The disbursement would then actually be signed and paid FROM Franklin2's own real wallet (self-transfer to itself in this specific 2-citizen case, but a genuine wrong-payer/ledger-corruption bug in general, and would corrupt every downstream repayment/default/interest calculation which is all keyed off lender_id/lender_wallet). No test in wake-gate.test.mjs constructs this exact scenario (env belonging to citizen X while selectedPair.lenderId resolves to citizen Y) -- every fixture's env either supplies TEST_LENDER_KEY directly or a deps.resolveLenderPrivateKey stub that trivially returns the 'right' key by fiat, never testing the real resolve-identity.mjs against a mismatched ANICCA_HOME.

additionalEvidence.note: defaultDisburse forwards deps.lenderPrivateKey to payViaFacilitator; provisionalRow.lender_wallet is populated from the registry's freshLender.walletAddress.evm; disburseResult (which includes payerAddress) is never cross-checked against lender_wallet before appending the final row
signAuthorization derives payer.address from the raw privateKey, independent of any caller-declared 'expected lender' identity

real production registry: exactly Franklin + Franklin2, each with its own distinct homeDir, confirming resolveLenderPrivateKey({env}) result depends entirely on WHICH instance's env the wake runs under
no fixture constructs 'caller env belongs to citizen X, selectedPair.lenderId resolves to citizen Y' -- the exact scenario this finding describes
